key_insight: A new preprocessing tool adapts hybrid unstructured meshes around immersed geometries so immersed boundary solvers can achieve accurate CFD on complex, partially body-fitted flow problems.
engineering_relevance: It enables efficient simulation of changing or multi-element aerodynamic configurations by combining body-fitted meshing for fixed parts with immersed boundary treatment for moving or difficult-to-mesh parts.
method: Starts from an external conforming hybrid background mesh with tetrahedra, hexahedra, prisms, and pyramids.
Refines the mesh locally around immersed geometries to improve resolution where the flow needs it most.
Applies the workflow to finite volume and discontinuous Galerkin solvers for Navier--Stokes and RANS simulations.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated on cylinder, NACA0012, and multi-element airfoil cases, with results reported to agree well with experimental data.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the initial background mesh and careful refinement near immersed surfaces to avoid accuracy or robustness issues.
paper_title: Mesh Adaptation on Hybrid Unstructured Meshes for Immersed Boundary Methods
